intro: Picture a small, quiet boutique hotel in a residential pocket of Lampang town: rooms bigger than the price suggests, every one with its own balcony, free parking right out front, and free coffee and toast in the morning — At Home Boutique is the place guests consistently praise for its large, clean rooms, its peace and quiet, its kind staff and its value. It's a small boutique hotel on Sooksawat 1 Road in the Phrabat area, from around THB 700/night · scoring 8.4 from roughly 197 real guest reviews on Trip.com and 4.3/5 on Tripadvisor · The one thing to know up front: it sits away from the Kad Kong Ta old town, so it suits self-drivers more than those who want to walk the old streets.

body.html: At Home Boutique sits on Sooksawat 1 Road in the Phrabat area of Lampang town — a quiet residential neighbourhood, not a busy tourist strip. The thing guests mention most is the calm and the rooms that are larger than the price suggests. It's a small boutique hotel that self-drivers pick often, thanks to free on-site parking and a location close to Lampang Airport, making it an easy base before driving into town for Kad Kong Ta or out to the temples beyond the city.

What guests agree on most is the spacious, clean Deluxe rooms of around 30 square metres. Many reviews say the rooms feel bigger than expected for a sub-THB-1,000 rate, with two desks, a comfortable bed, and a private balcony in every room. Rooms are air-conditioned with polished floors, a TV, fridge, minibar, kettle, free water and a walk-in hot shower. They're simply styled and feel private — and guests note that getting a room this spacious at this price is a real strong point for Lampang.
"Really large room, clean, very quiet, with a balcony and parking right outside the door. Kind, helpful staff and just over seven hundred baht — great value if you're driving your own car."

What sets At Home Boutique apart from similarly priced places is the small touches and the warm service. There are free bikes to borrow for riding around the neighbourhood, and free coffee and toast in the morning (though it's not a full breakfast). Free on-site parking is a genuine advantage here, the front desk is staffed 24 hours, and Wi-Fi is free throughout. Staff are a frequent highlight in reviews — guests describe the owner and team as kind, friendly and helpful, speaking both Thai and English.

Be clear about the location. At Home Boutique is in a residential part of town, a fair drive from the Kad Kong Ta old town and walking street. From here it's a short drive to Wat Sri Chum, Wat Pa Fang and Wat Si Rong Mueang, while Kad Kong Ta and the Wang River need a drive in. It's close to Lampang Airport, about 2 km away, which suits travellers flying into Lampang or passing through who want a quiet stay. In winter high season (November–February), this small hotel fills quickly because it has few rooms, so book ahead.

To be honest, the distance from the tourist areas is the main limitation here. The most common note in reviews is that the surroundings are quiet with little to do nearby, and you have to drive out for restaurants and convenience stores. Without your own car, getting into the old town is harder than from a Kad Kong Ta hotel. Some reviews also mention the bathroom can be short on basics like soap, so it's worth packing your own toiletries just in case.

Also worth knowing: there's no full breakfast and no pool. It's just free coffee and toast in the morning, so for a proper breakfast you'll drive out to a place in town. Overall this is a stay built around spacious, clean rooms, quiet, free parking and value — exactly what self-drivers who want a peaceful base on a budget are looking for, rather than somewhere you step out the door and find food and sights all around you.

In short, At Home Boutique suits travellers driving their own car who want a spacious, clean, quiet boutique room with free parking, at a budget price. If you're after somewhere walkable to Kad Kong Ta, a buffet breakfast, or a riverside resort with a pool, this isn't it. But if what you want is a spacious clean room with a balcony, real quiet, easy parking and a sub-THB-1,000 rate — it delivers that genuinely well.

A tip from following the reviews here: pack your own toiletries just in case, since some guests note the bathroom basics can be short, and plan to rely on your car, as the area is quiet and you'll drive out for meals. Borrow the free bikes for an evening ride around the neighbourhood. In winter, book ahead — rooms are few and fill fast — and always compare prices across platforms before booking.

honestSummary: At Home Boutique is best for travellers who drive their own car and want a spacious, clean, quiet boutique room with free parking, at a budget price. Its appeal is the roomy balconied rooms, the quiet, easy parking, free bikes and value — not a walk-to-Kad-Kong-Ta location or a big hotel with a pool. You'll need to accept that the location is away from the sights and needs a car, that there's no full breakfast, and that bathroom basics aren't always complete — but in return you get a spacious, clean, quiet room at a sub-THB-1,000 rate that's hard to find.
honestChecks: If you don't have a car and want to walk the old town — this is away from Kad Kong Ta and the walking street, so you'll drive in → a hotel in the Kad Kong Ta area will be far easier to explore on foot.
If you need breakfast at the hotel — there's no full breakfast here, only free coffee and toast → plan to drive out for a morning meal in town, or choose a stay that includes breakfast.
If you're particular about bathroom amenities — some reviews say soap and basics can be missing → pack your own toiletries so you don't have to go out to buy them.

faq.q: What are the rooms and atmosphere like at At Home Boutique?
faq.a: The highlight is Deluxe rooms of around 30 sqm, all with private balconies, clean, with AC, TV, fridge, minibar, hot water and a walk-in shower · There are free bikes to borrow, free coffee and toast in the morning, and free parking · The feel is a simple, clean, quiet boutique in a residential area, not a big hotel in a tourist zone.

faq.q: What should I know before staying at At Home Boutique?
faq.a: The notes that come up in reviews are that the location is away from Kad Kong Ta and the walking street so you drive into town, the surroundings are quiet with few restaurants, and there's no full breakfast (just free coffee and toast) · Some reviews say bathroom basics aren't always complete so pack your own, and there's no pool — which makes it better suited to self-drivers wanting a quiet stay.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book, and is cancellation free?
faq.a: In winter (November–February) book several weeks ahead, as it's Lampang's high season and the hotel has few rooms so it fills fast · Outside that, a few days ahead is usually fine · Every platform offers a Free Cancellation option — choose that if your plans aren't firm, and compare prices across platforms before booking.
